newsitem.title: USA: Range-bound natgas futures end near session lows.
newsitem.headline: Range-bound natgas futures end near session lows.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures settled mostly lower Tuesday due to technical selling and talk of cash prices below index levels, industry sources said.
October ended 3.8 cents lower at $1.821 per million British thermal units after falling to a low of $1.815 earlier. November broke through the $2 mark to finish down 3.6 cents at $1.979.

"It was just (technical) selling. Cash held in there for the most part, and people are no longer concerned about storage," said one trader, noting many have now put the stock situation on the backburner until the winter season begins.

Despite expectations for above- to much-above-normal temperatures in the deep Southwest, southern Florida, Northeast and the Great Lakes states this week, most are assuming temperatures will moderate as the month progresses, thereby putting downward pressure on prices.
Technically, traders were still holding onto the $1.82 support level in October. Resistance was seen first in the $1.93-1.95 area and then at $1.98.

Cash prices at the U.S. Gulf Coast pipes remained at about a 10-cent discount to futures in the low-$1.70s. However, late summer heat in the Northeast pushed New York city-gate prices to about $2.10, up from Friday's mid-$1.80s.
NYMEX said an estimated 16,597 Henry Hub contracts traded, up from Friday's revised tally of 10,748 but still well below the average.
The 12-month strip fell by 2.6 cents to $1.995.
The NYMEX October Permian contract finished the day untraded at $1.56.

On the KCBT, October also extended its losses late to finish three cents weaker at $1.60. Other months were flat to down 3.7 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.9 cent to 22.1 cents (NYMEX premium).
Physical prices at Waha remained at a discount to index levels in the mid-to-high $1.60s.
